candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — prevention, screening and health education
candidate.educational_objective: Classify an adult BMI of 32 kg/m² as Class 1 obesity while recognizing BMI as a screening measure that requires clinical context.

options.A: A BMI of 32 kg/m² falls in the CDC class 1 obesity screening category, but BMI should be interpreted with other clinical factors rather than used as a stand-alone diagnosis of health.
options.B: A BMI of 32 kg/m² falls in the overweight category because adult obesity begins only at 35 kg/m².
options.C: A BMI of 32 kg/m² by itself establishes the presence and severity of metabolic disease, so medical history and other risk factors add little information.
options.D: A BMI of 32 kg/m² is considered a healthy-weight value for adults because adult BMI categories depend mainly on age and sex.

candidate.rationale: CDC classifies adult BMI from 30.0 to less than 35.0 kg/m² as Class 1 obesity. CDC also describes BMI as a screening measure that should be considered along with other health information rather than as a stand-alone diagnosis. Thus A is the accurate interpretation.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Adult BMI 32 kg/m² is within the Class 1 obesity screening category, and BMI should be interpreted with other clinical information.
candidate.source_locator: Adult BMI Categories table — 30.0 to <35.0 kg/m² = Class 1 obesity; accompanying statement that BMI is a screening measure interpreted with other health information.
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.source_version_date: CDC page dated 2024-03-19; live page rechecked 2026-08-16.
candidate.stem: An adult client’s BMI is 32 kg/m². Which interpretation is most accurate?
